findings.claim: U.S. natural-gas prices are jointly conditioned by storage, seasonality, weather and physical supply-demand factors rather than by a single financial driver.
findings.expected_direction: tighter physical balance -> higher scarcity value and price pressure

findings.caveat: Magnitude is regime- and infrastructure-dependent; capacity availability must be separated from global price signals.
findings.claim: Growth of U.S. LNG exports creates a structural demand channel through which export capacity and feedgas demand can tighten the domestic gas balance.
findings.expected_direction: higher export/feedgas demand, holding supply fixed -> tighter domestic balance

findings.claim: At monthly frequency, real-time U.S. natural-gas price forecasts can outperform a no-change benchmark at several horizons extending to two years; futures-based forecasts, parsimonious fundamentals and forecast combinations are competitive, while the nearest horizon remains difficult.
findings.design_implication: Reproduce the monthly 1-24 month real-time forecasting result as its own fresh target family.
findings.expected_direction: forecastability is horizon-dependent and no single model dominates all horizons
